source_units.text: He who lives for ever created all things together.
The Lord alone will be justified.
He has empowered no one to declare His works fully; who will trace out His mighty deeds?
Who will count the might of His greatness? Who will go on to recount His mercies?
It is impossible to diminish or to add, and impossible to trace out the Lord’s wonders.
When a person finishes, then he begins; when he stops, then he will be at a loss.
What is a human being, and what is his use? What is his good, and what is his evil?
The number of a person’s days, in many years, is a hundred.
Like a drop of water from the sea or a grain of sand, so are a few years in a day of eternity.
Therefore the Lord was patient with them and poured His mercy upon them.
He saw and knew that their end was grievous; therefore He multiplied His atonement.
A person’s mercy is toward his neighbor, but the Lord’s mercy is upon all flesh: rebuking, disciplining, teaching, and bringing back like a shepherd his flock.
He has mercy on those who receive discipline and those who hasten eagerly toward His judgments.
Child, do not add reproach to good deeds, or the grief of words to any gift.
Will not dew bring relief from scorching heat? So a word is better than a gift.
Behold, is not a word beyond a good gift? Yet both are found with a gracious man.
A fool will reproach gracelessly, and a grudging person’s gift makes eyes waste away.
Learn before speaking, and attend to your health before illness.
Examine yourself before judgment, and at the hour of visitation you will find atonement.
Humble yourself before you fall ill, and show repentance at the time of sins.
Do not be held back from repaying a vow at the right time, and do not wait until death to be justified.
Prepare yourself before making a vow, and do not become like a person testing the Lord.
Remember wrath in the days of death, and the time of retribution when the face is turned away.
Remember a time of famine in a time of fullness, poverty and need in days of wealth.
From morning until evening the time changes, and all things are swift before the Lord.
A wise person will be cautious in everything, and in days of sins will guard against wrongdoing.
Every understanding person has known wisdom and will give acknowledgment to the one who finds her.
Those understanding in words have themselves become wise and rained down precise proverbs.
Do not walk after your desires, and restrain your appetites.
If you supply your soul with the satisfaction of desire, it will make you an object of your enemies’ gloating.
Do not rejoice in great luxury, lest you be bound to contribute to it.
Do not become poor by feasting on borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse.
A drunken worker will not become rich; the one who despises small things will fall little by little.
Wine and women will lead understanding men astray, and the one who clings to prostitutes will become more reckless.
Rot and worms will inherit him, and a reckless soul will be taken away.
The one who trusts quickly is lighthearted, and the one who sins will wrong his own soul.
The one who rejoices in heart will be condemned,
but the one who hates chatter diminishes evil.
Never repeat a word, and you will certainly lose nothing.
Do not tell it to friend or enemy, and unless silence is a sin for you, do not reveal it.
For someone has heard you and kept watch on you, and in time he will hate you.
Have you heard a word? Let it die with you. Take courage; it will certainly not make you burst.
A fool will suffer labor pains over a word, like a woman giving birth over her baby.
An arrow fixed in the flesh of a thigh—so is a word in a fool’s belly.
Question a friend; perhaps he did not do it, and if he did, question him so that he may not repeat it.
Question your neighbor; perhaps he did not say it, and if he has said it, question him so that he may not say it again.
Question a friend, for slander often occurs; do not trust every report.
There is someone who slips without intending it in his soul; who has not sinned with his tongue?
Question your neighbor before threatening him, and give place to the law of the Most High.
All wisdom is fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom there is doing the law.
Knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, and where sinners take counsel there is no prudence.
There is shrewdness that is an abomination, and there is a foolish person deficient in wisdom.
Better someone lacking understanding but full of fear than someone abounding in prudence who transgresses the law.
There is precise shrewdness that is unjust, and there is someone who twists matters in order to bring a judgment to light.
There is someone who acts wickedly while bowed down in gloom, with his inward parts full of deceit.
Hiding his face and pretending to be deaf, where he has not been recognized he will get ahead of you.
If lack of strength prevents him from sinning, he will do evil when he finds an opportunity.
A man will be recognized from his appearance, and an understanding person from the look of his face.
A man’s clothing, the grin of his teeth, and a person’s steps will declare what he is like.
There is a rebuke that is not fitting, and there is a silent person who is prudent.
How much better to rebuke than to be angry,
and the one who acknowledges his fault will be kept from loss.
A eunuch’s desire to take a young woman’s virginity—so is the one who carries out judgments by force.
There is a silent person who is found wise, and there is someone hated for much chatter.
There is someone silent because he has no answer, and someone silent because he knows the right time.
A wise person will keep silent until the right time, but a babbler and a fool will miss the right time.
The one who multiplies words will be loathed, and the one who assumes authority will be hated.
There is success for a man amid adversity, and there is a gain that brings loss.
There is a gift that will not benefit you, and a gift whose repayment is double.
There is loss for the sake of glory, and there is someone who has lifted his head from lowliness.
There is someone who buys much for little and pays for it sevenfold.
A wise person will make himself welcome by his words, but fools’ favors will be wasted.
An unthinking person’s gift will not benefit you, for his eyes seek many things in exchange for one.
He will give little and reproach much, and open his mouth like a herald. Today he will lend, and tomorrow he will demand repayment; such a person is hateful.
A fool will say, “I have no friend, and there is no gratitude for my good deeds.”
Those who eat his bread are base in speech. How often, and how many, will laugh at him?
Better a slip on the ground than a slip of the tongue; so the fall of the wicked will come swiftly.
A graceless person is an untimely tale; it will be continually in the mouth of the uninstructed.
A proverb will be rejected from a fool’s mouth, for he will certainly not say it at its proper time.
There is someone prevented from sinning by need; in his rest he will not be pierced with remorse.
There is someone who destroys his soul through shame, and through regard for a foolish face he will lose it.
There is someone who makes a promise to a friend because of shame, and has acquired him as an enemy for nothing.
A lie is an evil blemish in a person; it will be continually in the mouth of the uninstructed.
A thief is preferable to someone who persists in lying, but both will inherit destruction.
A lying person’s character is dishonor, and his shame is continually with him.
A wise person will advance himself through his words, and a prudent man will please dignitaries.
The one who works the land will raise his heap of grain, and the one who pleases dignitaries will atone for injustice.
Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise and turn aside rebukes like a muzzle in the mouth.
Hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure—what benefit is there in either?
Better a person who hides his foolishness than a person who hides his wisdom.
Child, have you sinned? Do not add to it any more, and pray concerning your earlier sins.
Flee from sin as from the presence of a snake, for if you approach it, it will bite you. Its teeth are lions’ teeth, destroying human lives.
All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword; there is no healing for its wound.
Intimidation and insolence will lay wealth waste; so the house of a proud person will be laid waste.
A poor person’s petition goes from his mouth to His ears, and His judgment comes swiftly.
The one who hates rebuke is in a sinner’s tracks, but the one who fears the Lord will turn back in heart.
One who is powerful with the tongue is known from far away, but an understanding person knows when he slips.
The one who builds his house with others’ money is like someone gathering its stones for a storm.
An assembly of the lawless is gathered tow, and their end is a flame of fire.
The sinners’ road is smoothed with stones, but at its end is the pit of Hades.
The one who keeps the law masters his thoughts, and wisdom is the fulfillment of the fear of the Lord.
The one who is not shrewd will not be instructed, yet there is a shrewdness that multiplies bitterness.
A wise person’s knowledge will increase like a flood, and his counsel is like a spring of life.
A fool’s inward parts are like a broken vessel; he will retain no knowledge.
If a knowledgeable person hears a wise word, he will praise it and add to it. A self-indulgent person heard it, and it displeased him; he cast it behind his back.
A fool’s explanation is like a burden on a journey, but grace will be found on an understanding person’s lip.
The mouth of a prudent person will be sought in the assembly, and they will consider his words in their heart.
Wisdom is like a ruined house to a fool, and an uncomprehending person’s knowledge is unexamined words.
Instruction is fetters on the feet of the senseless, and like handcuffs on his right hand.
A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a shrewd man will barely smile quietly.
Instruction is like a golden ornament to the prudent, and like a bracelet on his right arm.
A fool’s foot is quick to enter a house, but an experienced person will feel shame before it.
A foolish person peers into a house from its door, but an instructed man will stand outside.
It is a person’s lack of instruction to listen at a door, but the prudent will feel weighed down by the dishonor.
Strangers’ lips will talk about these things, but the words of the prudent will be weighed in a balance.
Fools have their heart in their mouth, but the heart of the wise is their mouth.
When an ungodly person curses Satan, he curses his own soul.
The whisperer stains his own soul and will be hated where he dwells.
A lazy person has been compared to a filthy stone, and everyone will hiss at his dishonor.
A lazy person has been compared to a lump of dung; everyone who picks it up will shake his hand.
A father’s shame is in begetting an uninstructed child, and a daughter brings about loss.
A prudent daughter will inherit her husband, but one who brings shame brings grief to her parent.
A shameless woman shames both father and husband and will be dishonored by both.
An untimely discourse is music in mourning, but lashes and discipline are wisdom at every time.
The one teaching a fool is gluing a potsherd together, waking a sleeper from deep sleep.
The one speaking to a fool is speaking to someone drowsy; at the end he will say, “What is it?”

Weep over a dead person, for he has lost the light; weep also over a fool, for he has lost understanding. Weep more gently over the dead, because he has found rest, but the fool’s life is worse than death.
Mourning for the dead lasts seven days; for a fool and an ungodly person, all the days of his life.

Do not multiply words with a fool or go to someone without understanding. Guard against him so that you do not have trouble, and you will certainly not be stained by what he shakes off. Turn away from him, and you will find rest and will certainly not grow weary of his madness.
What is heavier than lead? What is its name except a fool?
Sand, salt, and a lump of iron are easier to bear than a person without understanding.
A wooden bond fitted into a building will not be loosened in a shaking; so a heart established on thoughtful counsel will not be cowardly when the time comes.
A heart made firm upon an understanding thought is like a sanded ornament on a polished wall.
Stakes set on a height will certainly not endure before the wind; so a cowardly heart resting on a foolish thought will certainly not endure before any fear.
The one who pricks an eye will bring down tears; the one who pricks a heart reveals feeling.
Throwing a stone at birds drives them away, and the one who reproaches a friend will break up friendship.
If you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back.

If you open your mouth against a friend, do not be afraid, for there is reconciliation—except for reproach, pride, disclosure of a secret, and a treacherous blow; at these things every friend will flee.
Establish trust with your neighbor in poverty, so that you may be filled together with him in his good circumstances. Stay with him in a time of affliction, so that you may share his inheritance.
Before fire come a furnace’s vapor and smoke; so before bloodshed come insults.
I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend, and I will certainly not hide from his face.
If evil things happen to me because of him, everyone who hears will guard against him.
Who will place a guard upon my mouth and a skillful seal upon my lips, so that I do not fall because of it and my tongue destroy me?
Lord, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel; do not let me fall through them.
Who will set lashes over my thought and wisdom’s discipline over my heart, so that they may not spare my errors of ignorance, and He may certainly not pass over their sins,
so that my errors of ignorance do not multiply and my sins increase, and I fall before my adversaries and my enemy gloat over me?
Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me haughty eyes,
and turn desire away from me.
Do not let the appetite of the belly and sexual intercourse overtake me, and do not hand me over to a shameless soul.
Listen, children, to discipline of the mouth; the one who keeps it will certainly not be caught.
A sinner will be caught by his lips, and an abusive person and a proud person will stumble through them.
Do not accustom your mouth to an oath, and do not make a habit of naming the Holy One.
For just as a household slave under continual examination will not be free of bruises, so the one who continually swears and invokes the name will certainly not be cleansed from sin.

A man of many oaths will be filled with lawlessness, and a scourge will not depart from his house. If he offends, his sin is upon him; if he disregards it, he has sinned twice. If he swore in vain, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with calamities.
There is an expression comparable to death; let it not be found in Jacob’s inheritance. For all these things will depart from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins.
Do not accustom your mouth to crude ignorance, for sinful speech is in it.

Remember your father and mother, for you sit among dignitaries, lest you forget yourself before them and become foolish through your habit; then you will wish you had not been born and curse the day of your birth.
A person accustomed to words of reproach will certainly not be instructed throughout all his days.
Two kinds multiply sins, and the third will bring wrath:

a heated soul, like a burning fire, will certainly not be quenched until it is consumed; a sexually immoral man in his fleshly body will certainly not stop until he kindles a fire. Every loaf is sweet to a sexually immoral man; he will certainly not cease until he dies.

A man who transgresses from his marriage bed says in his soul, “Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and the walls cover me; no one sees me. What should I fear? The Most High will certainly not remember my sins.”
Human eyes are what he fears; he does not know that the Lord’s eyes are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, surveying every human way and observing hidden places.
Before all things were created, they were known to Him, and likewise after they were completed.
This man will receive retribution in the city’s squares and be seized where he did not suspect it.
So also a woman who leaves her husband and presents an heir from another man.
For first she disobeyed the law of the Most High; second she wronged her husband; and third she committed adultery in sexual immorality and presented children from another man.
She will be brought before the assembly, and there will be a visitation upon her children.
Her children will not spread out into a root, and her branches will not bear fruit.
She will leave her memory as a curse, and her reproach will not be erased.
Those left behind will know that nothing is better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing sweeter than attending to the Lord’s commandments.
Wisdom will praise her own soul and boast in the midst of her people.
She will open her mouth in the assembly of the Most High and boast before His host:
“I came forth from the mouth of the Most High and covered the earth like mist.
I dwelt in the heights, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.
Alone I encircled heaven’s circuit and walked in the depth of the abysses.
In the waves of the sea, in all the earth, and in every people and nation I gained possession.
Among all these I sought rest, and in whose inheritance I might lodge.
Then the Creator of all commanded me; my Creator settled my tent and said, ‘Dwell in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel.’
Before the age, from the beginning, He created me, and for ever I will certainly not cease.
I ministered before Him in the holy tent, and thus I was established in Zion.
Likewise He settled me in the beloved city, and my authority was in Jerusalem.
I took root in a glorified people, in the Lord’s portion, His inheritance.
I rose high like a cedar in Lebanon, like a cypress in the mountains of Hermon.
I rose high like a palm in En-gedi, like rose plants in Jericho, like a stately olive in the plain; I rose high like a plane tree.
Like cinnamon and aromatic aspalathus I gave a scent; like choice myrrh I spread fragrance, like galbanum, onycha, and stacte, and like a cloud of frankincense in a tent.
Like a terebinth I spread out my branches, and my branches were branches of glory and grace.
Like a vine I sprouted grace, and my blossoms were fruit of glory and wealth.
Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled from my produce.
For my memory is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than a honeycomb.
Those who eat me will still hunger, and those who drink me will still thirst.
The one who obeys me will not be ashamed, and those who work in me will not sin.”
All these things are the book of the covenant of God Most High, the law which Moses commanded us as an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob,
which fills with wisdom like the Pishon, like the Tigris in the days of new crops,
which fills with understanding like the Euphrates, like the Jordan in the days of harvest,
which makes instruction appear like light, like the Gihon in the days of vintage.
The first did not come to know her fully, and likewise the last did not trace her out.
For her thought grew abundant from the sea, and her counsel from a great abyss.
I too came out like a channel from a river, like a watercourse into a garden.
I said, “I will water my garden and drench my garden bed.” Then behold, my channel became a river, and my river became a sea.
I will again make instruction shine like the dawn and reveal these things far away.
I will again pour out teaching like prophecy and leave it for generations of ages.
See that I have labored not for myself alone, but for all who seek her.
In three things I was adorned and stood beautiful before the Lord and human beings: harmony among brothers, friendship among neighbors, and a wife and husband living agreeably with one another.
But my soul hated three kinds, and I was greatly offended at their life: a proud poor person, a rich liar, and an old adulterer deficient in understanding.
You have not gathered in youth; how could you find anything in your old age?
How fitting is judgment for gray hair, and knowledge of counsel for elders!
How fitting is wisdom for the old, and thought and counsel for the honored!
Long experience is the crown of the old, and their boast is the fear of the Lord.
Nine things I considered happy in my heart, and the tenth I will speak with my tongue: a person rejoicing in children, one who lives to see his enemies’ fall;
happy is the one who lives with an understanding wife, who has not slipped with his tongue, and who has not served someone unworthy of him;
happy is the one who has found prudence and the one who speaks into listening ears.
How great is the one who has found wisdom! Yet he is not above the one who fears the Lord.
The fear of the Lord has surpassed everything; to whom will the one who holds it fast be compared?
Any wound, but not a wound of the heart; any evil, but not a woman’s evil;
any calamity, but not a calamity from those who hate; any retribution, but not the retribution of enemies.
There is no head beyond a snake’s head, and no anger beyond an enemy’s anger.
I would choose to live with a lion and a dragon rather than live with an evil woman.
A woman’s evil changes her appearance and darkens her face like a bear.
Her husband will recline among his neighbors and involuntarily groan bitterly.
Every evil is small beside a woman’s evil; may a sinner’s lot fall upon her.
A sandy ascent under an old person’s feet—so is a talkative wife to a quiet husband.
Do not fall for a woman’s beauty, and do not long for a woman.
Wrath, shamelessness, and great shame result if a wife supplies her husband.
An evil wife is a humbled heart, a gloomy face, and a wound of the heart; one who will not make her husband happy is slack hands and paralyzed knees.
From a woman came the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die.
Do not give water an outlet, or an evil wife freedom of speech.
If she does not walk according to your direction, cut her off from your flesh.

context_units.text: “God of the fathers and Lord of mercy, who made all things by Thy word
and by Thy wisdom fashioned the human being, so that he might rule over the creatures made by Thee
and administer the world in holiness and righteousness, and render judgment in uprightness of soul,
give me wisdom, who sits beside Thy thrones, and do not reject me from among Thy servants.
For I am Thy slave and the son of Thy slave woman, a weak and short-lived human being, deficient in understanding judgment and laws.
For even if someone is perfect among the sons of human beings, without the wisdom that comes from Thee, he will be reckoned as nothing.
What, then, is the Jew’s advantage, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
Much in every way. First, indeed, because they were entrusted with the oracles of God.
For what if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness nullify God’s faithfulness?
May it never be! But let God be true, and every human being a liar, just as it is written, “So that Thou mayest be justified in Thy words, and wilt prevail when Thou art judged.”
But if our unrighteousness demonstrates God’s righteousness, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous when He brings wrath? I speak in human terms.
May it never be! For then how will God judge the world?
For He is wise in understanding, mighty and great. Who grew hard against Him and endured?
He wears the mountains out, and they do not know; He overturns them in anger.
He shakes the world beneath heaven from its foundations, and its pillars sway.
He speaks to the sun and it does not rise, and He seals up the stars.
He alone stretched out heaven and walks on the sea as on ground.
He makes the Pleiades, the Evening Star, and Arcturus, and the storehouses of the south.
He does great and unsearchable things, glorious and extraordinary things beyond numbering.
If He passes over me, I will not see; if He passes by me, even then I do not perceive Him.
If He takes away, who will turn Him back? Who will say to Him, ‘What hast Thou done?’
A praise of David. I will exalt Thee, my God, my King, and bless Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.
Every day I will bless Thee and praise Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.
Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; His greatness has no limit.
Generation after generation will praise Thy works, and they will declare Thy power.
They will speak of the magnificence of the glory of Thy holiness, and they will recount Thy wonders.
They will speak of the power of Thy fearsome acts, and they will recount Thy greatness.
They will pour forth remembrance of the abundance of Thy kindness and rejoice in Thy righteousness.
Compassionate and merciful is the Lord, patient and abundant in mercy.
The Lord is kind to all, and His compassions are over all His works.
Let all Thy works give thanks unto Thee, Lord, and let Thy holy ones bless Thee.
They will speak of the glory of Thy kingdom and tell of Thy might,
to make known to the sons of men Thy might and the glory of the magnificence of Thy kingdom.
Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and Thy lordship endures through every generation.
I saw the distraction God has given human beings to be distracted by.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also put the age in their hearts, so that human beings may not find out the work God has done from beginning to end.
I knew that there is no good for them except to rejoice and do good during one’s life.
Moreover, whenever a person eats and drinks and sees good in all his toil, this is God’s gift.
I knew that everything God has done will endure for ever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it; God has done this so that people may fear before Him.
What has come to be already is, and whatever is to come has already come to be; God will seek the one who is pursued.
For I will see the heavens, works of Thy fingers, the moon and stars which Thou didst found:
what is a human being, that Thou rememberest him, or a son of man, that Thou visitest him?
Thou madest him a little lower than angels; Thou didst crown him with glory and honor,
and didst appoint him over the works of Thy hands; Thou didst subject everything beneath his feet:
A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, Thou becamest our refuge through every generation.
Before the mountains came to be and the earth and inhabited world were formed, from age to age Thou art.
Do not turn a man toward humiliation; and Thou saidst, Return, sons of men.
For a thousand years in Thine eyes are like yesterday, which passed, and a watch in the night.
Their things counted as nothing will be years. In the morning, like green grass, may it pass away;
in the morning may it blossom and pass away; in the evening may it fall, grow hard and dry up.
For we failed in Thine anger and were troubled in Thy wrath.
Thou didst set our lawless deeds before Thee; our age is in the light of Thy face.
For all our days failed, and in Thine anger we failed; I pondered our years like a spider.
The days of our years—in them are seventy years, or, with strength, eighty years; the greater part of them is toil and pain, for gentleness came upon us, and we shall be disciplined.
Who knows the might of Thine anger, and Thy wrath from the fear of Thee?
So make known how to number Thy right hand, and those bound in heart in wisdom.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.
He will not be angry to the end, nor maintain wrath for ever.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our lawless deeds,
for according to heaven’s height above the earth, the Lord strengthened His mercy toward those who fear Him.
As far as the east is distant from the west, He removed our lawless deeds from us.
As a father has compassion on children, the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,
for He knew our formation. Remember that we are dust.
A man—his days are like grass; like a flower of the field, so he will flower,
for a wind passed through him, and he will not exist, and he will no longer recognize his place.
But the Lord’s mercy is from eternity to eternity toward those who fear Him, and His righteousness toward children’s children,
to those who keep His covenant and remember His commandments to do them.
In all these things they sinned still and did not believe in His wonders,
and their days failed in futility, and their years with haste.
Whenever He killed them, they sought Him; and they returned and rose early toward God,
and remembered that God is their helper, and God Most High is their redeemer.
And they deceived Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue,
but their heart was not upright with Him, nor were they faithful in His covenant.
But He is compassionate; He will make atonement for their sins and not destroy, and will turn back His wrath again and again, and will not kindle all His anger.
And He remembered that they are flesh, a spirit going away and not returning.
Son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline or lose heart when corrected by Him,
for the Lord disciplines the one He loves and scourges every son He receives.
Blessed is the person who found wisdom, the mortal who saw good sense,
for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
For length of life and years of living are in her right hand, and wealth and glory in her left.
Righteousness proceeds from her mouth, and she carries law and mercy on her tongue.
Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
She is a tree of life to all who hold her fast, and secure for those who lean on her as on the Lord.
Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter trials of various kinds,
knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,
a man of divided mind, unstable in all his ways.
A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son sneers at his mother.
The paths of a senseless person lack understanding, but an intelligent man walks making his course straight.
Those who do not honor councils put plans off, but counsel remains in the hearts of those who deliberate.
The evil person will certainly not heed it, nor say anything timely and good for the community.
The thoughts of an understanding person are ways of life, so that, turning aside from Hades, he may be saved.
The Lord pulls down the houses of the insolent, but He established the boundary of a widow.
An unjust thought is an abomination to the Lord, but the sayings of pure people are noble.
One who takes bribes destroys himself, but one who hates taking gifts is saved.
By acts of mercy and faithfulness sins are thoroughly cleansed, and by the fear of the Lord everyone turns from evil.
The hearts of the righteous meditate on faithful things, but the mouth of the impious answers evil things.
The ways of righteous men are acceptable to the Lord, and through them even enemies become friends.
God is far distant from the impious, but He listens to the prayers of the righteous.
Do not dine with a begrudging man, and do not desire his foods,
for as if someone swallowed a hair, so he eats and drinks.
Do not bring him in to yourself and eat your morsel with him, for he will vomit it and ruin your good words.
Say nothing into a fool’s ears, lest he sneer at your intelligent words.
One who answers a word before hearing it—it is foolishness and reproach for him.
An intelligent attendant calms a man’s anger, but who will bear a fainthearted man?
An intelligent heart acquires discernment, and the ears of the wise seek reflection.
Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord’s cup unworthily will be answerable for the Lord’s body and blood.
Let a person examine himself, and in this way let him eat from the bread and drink from the cup.
For the one who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment upon himself.
For this reason many among you are weak and ill, and a considerable number are asleep.
But if we discerned ourselves, we would not be judged.
Yet when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined, so that we may not be condemned with the world.
“And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.
Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?
Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring out a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
For a dream comes with much distraction, and a fool’s voice with many words.
Whenever you vow a vow to God, do not delay paying it, for there is no delight in fools. Pay whatever you vow.
Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.
Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before God, “It was ignorance,” lest God become angry at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.
For with many dreams come futilities and many words; therefore fear God.
A double weight is an abomination to the Lord, and deceitful scales are not good before Him.
A man’s steps are directed by the Lord, but how could a mortal understand his ways?
It is a trap for a man quickly to consecrate something of his own, for after making the vow comes reconsideration.
A wise king is a winnower of the impious, and will bring a wheel upon them.
The breath of human beings is the light of the Lord, who searches the store-chambers of the belly.
Or do you despise the wealth of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
But by your hardness and unrepentant heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of God’s righteous judgment,
who will repay each according to his works:
to those who, through perseverance in good work, seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, eternal life;
but to those acting from selfish ambition, who disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury,
affliction and distress upon every human soul that does evil—the Jew first and also the Greek;
but glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
For there is no partiality with God.
“Now therefore seek out a prudent and discerning man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
“And let Pharaoh act, and appoint governors over the land; and let them take a fifth of all the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
“And let them gather all the food of these seven good years which are coming; and let the grain be gathered under Pharaoh’s hand, and let food be kept in the cities.
“And the food shall be kept for the land against the seven years of famine which shall be in the land of Egypt, and the land shall not be destroyed by the famine.”
Do not boast of things for tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day will bear.
Let your neighbor praise you, and not your mouth, another, and not your lips.
A stone is heavy and sand hard to carry, but a fool’s anger is heavier than both.
There is a way that seems upright to people, but its final outcome comes to the bottom of Hades.
In gladness sorrow does not mingle, but in the end joy comes to mourning.
One rash in heart will be filled from his own ways, but a good man from his own thoughts.
The innocent person believes every word, but the resourceful comes to reconsideration.
The wise, becoming afraid, turned from evil, but the fool, trusting himself, mixes with a lawless person.
One quick to anger acts without counsel, but an intelligent man endures many things.
Besides becoming wise, Ecclesiastes also taught the people knowledge; and an ear will trace out an orderly arrangement of proverbs.
Ecclesiastes sought much to find words of delight and something written in uprightness, words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads and like planted nails, which were given from collections, from one shepherd, and something beyond them.
My son, beware of making many books; there is no limit, and much study is weariness of the flesh.
The conclusion of the matter—the whole is heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole human being.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, concerning everything overlooked, whether good or evil.
But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will certainly not fulfill the desire of the flesh.
For the flesh desires what is against the Spirit, and the Spirit what is against the flesh; for these oppose one another, so that you do not do the things you want.
But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under law.
Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, licentiousness,
idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambitions, divisions, factions,
envies, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these. I tell you beforehand, just as I told you before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law.
And those who belong to Christ Jesus crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
So also reckon yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires;
Do not present the parts of your body to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and the parts of your body to God as weapons of righteousness.
For sin will not rule over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.
Listen, son, and become wise, and straighten the reflections of your heart.
Do not be a wine-drinker, and do not stretch yourself over contributions and purchases of meat;
for every drunkard and frequenter of prostitutes will become poor, and every sleepy person will clothe himself in torn and ragged things.
Listen, son, to the father who begot you, and do not despise your mother because she has grown old.
My words have been spoken by God, an oracle concerning a king whom his mother instructed.
What will you keep, child? What? God’s sayings. Firstborn, I speak to you, son. What, child of my womb? What, child of my vows?
Do not give women your wealth, or your mind and livelihood to belated counsel.
Do everything with counsel; drink wine with counsel. The powerful are hot-tempered, but let them not drink wine,
so that, after drinking, they may not forget wisdom and become entirely unable to judge the weak rightly.
Give intoxicating drink to those in grief, and wine to drink to those in pain,
so that they may forget their poverty and no longer remember their troubles.
Open your mouth for God’s word, and judge everyone soundly.
Open your mouth and judge justly, and decide the case of the poor and weak.
He is light upon the surface of water; may their portion upon the earth be cursed.
May their plants appear dried up upon the earth, for they snatched an armful from orphans.
Then sin remembered him, and he vanished like a mist of dew. May what he did be repaid to him, and may every unjust person be crushed like incurable wood.
For he did no good to a barren woman and had no mercy on a woman,
and in anger he overthrew the powerless. Therefore, when he rises, he will certainly have no confidence concerning his own life;
Righteous lips conceal enmity, but those who bring forth abuse are most foolish.
Through much talking you will not escape sin, but by sparing your lips you will be intelligent.
The tongue of the righteous is fire-tested silver, but the heart of the impious will fail.
The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but fools die in want.
One lacking understanding sneers at citizens, but an intelligent man keeps quiet.
A double-tongued man reveals plans in a council, but one faithful in breath conceals matters.
Those who have no steering fall like leaves, but deliverance is in much counsel.
A man who wishes to separate from friends seeks pretexts, and at every time he will be subject to reproach.
One lacking understanding has no use for wisdom, for he is led rather by foolishness.
When the impious comes into the depth of evils, he despises, and dishonor and reproach come upon him.
A word in a man’s heart is deep water, and a river springs up, a fountain of life.
If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.
But if he does not hear, take one or two more with you, so that every matter may be established upon the mouth of two or three witnesses.
If he refuses to hear them, tell the Church. And if he refuses to hear even the Church, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.
Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.
For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in speech, that person is a complete man, able to bridle his whole body also.
Now if we put bits into horses’ mouths so that they obey us, we guide their whole body also.
Look also at ships: although so large and driven by harsh winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the pilot intends.
So also the tongue is a small member and boasts great things. Look how small a fire sets so great a forest ablaze!
And the tongue is a fire. The tongue is established among our members as a world of unrighteousness, staining the whole body, setting the wheel of life ablaze, and itself set ablaze by Gehenna.
For every kind of wild animal and bird, of creeping creature and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind;
but no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made in God’s likeness.
From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way.
Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening?
My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet water.
You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.
You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbour, and you shall not bear sin because of him.
And your hand shall not take vengeance, neither shall you remain angry with the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself; I am the Lord.
But where was wisdom found, and what is the place of understanding?
It has escaped every human and was hidden from the birds of heaven.
Destruction and Death said, ‘We have heard its renown.’
God established its way well, and He knows its place.
For He observes the whole realm under heaven, knowing everything in the earth that He made:
the weight of winds and measures of water;
when He acted in this way, He counted rain and a path for sounds amid a shaking.
Then He saw wisdom and expounded it; having prepared it, He traced it out.
And He said to a human, ‘Behold, reverence for God is wisdom, and abstaining from evils is knowledge.’”
Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show his works by good conduct in the gentleness of wisdom.
But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast against the truth and lie against it.
This is not the wisdom coming down from above; it is earthly, merely natural, demonic.
For where there are jealousy and selfish ambition, there are disorder and every foul practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, open to persuasion, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, without hypocrisy.
And a fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.
Silver given with deceit must be regarded like a potsherd; smooth lips cover a painful heart.
A weeping enemy agrees to everything with his lips, but in his heart devises deceits;
if the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded, for seven evils are in his life.
One who hides enmity establishes deceit, but one well known in councils discloses his own sins.
One who digs a pit for his neighbor will fall into it, and one who rolls a stone rolls it upon himself.
A false tongue hates truth, but an unrestrained mouth makes disorders.
They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.
They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

Therefore thus says the Lord: “Look, I am planning calamities against this tribe, from which you will certainly not lift your necks, and you will certainly not suddenly walk upright, for it is an evil time.
Who knows wise people, and who knows the solution of a saying? A person’s wisdom will light up his face, but one with a shameless face will be hated.
Guard the king’s mouth; and concerning the word of an oath of God, do not hurry.
You will go from his presence. Do not stand in an evil matter, for he will do whatever he pleases,
just as a king with authority speaks; and who will say to him, “What will you do?”
Whoever keeps a command will know no evil word, and a wise heart knows a time of judgment.
One who refrains from sending forth a harsh word is discerning, and a patient man is intelligent.
Wisdom will be reckoned to a senseless person who asks for wisdom, and someone who makes himself mute will seem intelligent.
And this is the message we have heard from Him and announce to you: God is light, and there is no darkness at all in Him.
If we say that we have fellowship with Him while walking in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
But if we walk in the light, as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from every sin.
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him a liar, and His word is not in us.
For all things there is a time, and a season for every matter beneath heaven.
a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted,
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to pull down and a time to build,
a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to beat the breast in mourning and a time to dance,
a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to keep far from embracing,
a time to seek and a time to lose, a time to keep and a time to throw away,
a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
a time to love and a time to hate, a time of war and a time of peace.
If the snake bites without a whispered charm, there is no advantage for the charmer.
The words of a wise person’s mouth are gracious, but a fool’s lips will drown him.
The beginning of his mouth’s words is folly, and the end of his speech is evil wandering.
The fool multiplies words. A person did not know what happened, and who will tell him what will be after him?
There is a sickness I have seen beneath the sun: wealth kept by its possessor to his harm,
and that wealth will be lost through a grievous distraction, and he fathered a son with nothing in his hand.
As he came naked from his mother’s womb, he will return to depart as he came. He will take nothing from his toil to carry in his hand.
This too is a grievous sickness: just as he came, so he will depart. What surplus has he from toiling for the wind?
All his days are in darkness and mourning, with much anger, sickness and wrath.
But He gives greater grace. Therefore it says, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
Submit yourselves therefore to God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, you of divided mind.
Be wretched and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into dejection.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.
Remove walking from legs, and a proverb from the mouth of fools.
One who binds a stone in a sling is like one who gives glory to a fool.
Thorns grow in the hand of the drunkard, but slavery is in the hand of fools.
Insolence brings a man low, but the Lord supports the humble-minded with glory.
One who shares with a thief hates his own life; but if, when an oath is set before them, those who heard do not report,
having feared and felt shame before people, they were tripped up; but one who trusts in the Lord will rejoice. Impiety gives a man a fall; but one who trusts in the Master will be saved.
Many court the faces of leaders, but what is just for a man comes from the Lord.
Deceit is in the heart of one devising evil things, but those who desire peace will rejoice.
Nothing unjust will please the righteous, but the impious will be filled with evils.
Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but one who performs faithful deeds is acceptable to Him.
An understanding man is a throne of discernment, but the heart of fools will meet curses.
I turned and lifted my eyes and saw: look, a flying sickle!
He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a flying sickle, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.”
He said to me, “This is the curse going out over the whole earth, because every thief will be punished by this with death, and every false swearer will be punished by this with death.

I will bring it out, says the Lord Almighty. It will enter the thief’s house and the house of whoever swears falsely by My name; it will lodge within his house and destroy it completely, its timbers and its stones.”
Every idle person is amid desires, but the hands of the courageous are engaged in care.
The righteous hates an unjust word, but the impious is ashamed and will have no frankness.
Righteousness guards the innocent, but sin makes the impious worthless.
An oracle is on the lips of a king, and his mouth will certainly not go astray in judgment.
The balance’s inclination is righteousness before the Lord, and His works are just weights.
One who does evil is an abomination to a king, for a throne of rule is prepared with righteousness.
Righteous lips are acceptable to a king, and he loves upright words.
A king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease him.
In the light of life is a king’s son, and those acceptable to him are like a cloud of late rain.
Nests of wisdom are more desirable than gold, and nests of understanding more desirable than silver.
Better is a man in dishonor who serves himself than one who clothes himself in honor but needs bread.
The righteous has compassion on the lives of his animals, but the inward affections of the impious are merciless.
One who works his own land will be filled with loaves, but those who pursue empty things lack understanding.
One who delights in time spent over wine will leave dishonor in his own strongholds.
The desires of the impious are evil, but the roots of the devout are in strongholds.
Through the sin of lips a sinner falls into traps, but the righteous escapes from them.
You shall not pervert the judgment of a poor man in his cause.
You shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, neither shall you justify the ungodly for gifts.
And you shall receive no gifts; for gifts blind the eyes of those who see, and corrupt righteous words.
And you shall not afflict a resident foreigner; for you know the soul of the resident foreigner, since you yourselves were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
Children, preserve instruction in peace. But hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure—what benefit is there in either?
A person who hides his foolishness is better than a person who hides his wisdom.
Therefore, be ashamed in accordance with my word. For it is not good to preserve every kind of shame, and not everything finds approval with everyone in good faith.
They call the wise and understanding worthless, but those sweet in speech will hear more.
Reflection is a fountain of life to those who possess it, but the discipline of fools is evil.
A wise person’s heart will understand what comes from his own mouth, and will carry discernment upon his lips.
Good words are honeycombs, and their sweetness is healing of the life.
Why are earth and ashes proud? For even in life I have cast out his entrails.
A long illness—the physician mocks it. A king today, and tomorrow he will die.
For when a person dies, he will inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.
A golden apple on a carnelian necklace—so is speaking a word.
A costly carnelian is fastened into a golden earring—a wise word into a receptive ear.
As snow coming forth benefits people in harvest heat, so a faithful messenger benefits those who sent him; for he benefits the lives of those who employ him.
Like winds and clouds and very conspicuous rains, so are those who boast of a false gift.
In patience is prosperity for kings, and a soft tongue crushes bones.
You will seek wisdom among evil people and not find it, but discernment is readily found among intelligent people.
Everything is against a foolish man, but wise lips are weapons of discernment.
The wisdom of resourceful people will recognize their ways, but the senselessness of fools is in wandering.
The one who reveals secrets has destroyed trust and will certainly not find a friend close to his soul.
Love a friend and keep faith with him; but if you reveal his secrets, do not pursue him afterward.
For as a person has lost his dead, so you have lost your neighbor’s friendship.
As you have released a bird from your hand, so you have let your neighbor go, and you will not catch him.
Do not pursue him, because he has gone far away and escaped like a gazelle from a trap.
For a wound can be bound up, and there is reconciliation after abuse, but the one who revealed secrets has lost hope.
Child, shed tears over the dead and begin a lament as one suffering terribly. Lay out his body according to his due, and do not neglect his burial.
Make your weeping bitter and your lament fervent; mourn according to his worth for one day or two because of slander, and be comforted because of grief.
For death comes from grief, and grief of heart will bend strength.
In calamity grief also remains, and the poor person’s life weighs upon the heart.
Do not give your heart over to grief; put it away, remembering the last things.
Do not forget: there is no return. You will not benefit this person, and you will harm yourself.
“Remember my judgment, for yours is likewise: yesterday for me, today for you.”
When the dead person rests, bring his remembrance to rest, and be comforted concerning him when his spirit departs.
Child, choose instruction from your youth, and until your hair is gray you will find wisdom.
Approach her like one who plows and sows, and wait for her good fruits. For you will labor a little in her cultivation and soon eat from her produce.
How very harsh she is to the uninstructed! The fainthearted will not remain with her.
She will be upon him like a heavy testing stone, and he will not delay throwing her away.
For wisdom is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many.
Listen, child, and receive my judgment; do not reject my counsel.
Put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her collar.
Place your shoulder beneath her and carry her, and do not resent her bonds.
Approach her with all your soul, and keep her ways with your whole strength.
Trace her out and seek her, and she will become known to you; when you have gained hold of her, do not let her go.
For in the end you will find her rest, and she will turn to gladness for you.
Her fetters will become a strong shelter for you, and her collars a robe of glory.
For there is a golden ornament upon her, and her bonds are a blue thread.
You will put her on as a robe of glory and place a crown of rejoicing upon yourself.
The fear of the Lord is glory and a boast, gladness and a crown of rejoicing.
The fear of the Lord will delight the heart and give gladness, joy, and length of days.
It will go well at the end with the one who fears the Lord, and on the day of his death he will be blessed.
To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; she was created together with the faithful in the womb.
Among human beings she nested on an eternal foundation, and among their offspring she will be trusted.
To fear the Lord is the fullness of wisdom, and she intoxicates them with her fruits.
She will fill their whole house with desirable things and their storehouses with her produce.
The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom, making peace and the health of healing flourish.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money,
saying, “Give me this authority too, so that anyone upon whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”
But Peter said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could acquire the gift of God with money!
You have neither part nor allotted share in this matter, for your heart is not upright before God.
Repent, therefore, of this wickedness of yours, and plead with the Lord that perhaps the intention of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that you are in bitter gall and a bond of unrighteousness.”
Simon answered, “You yourselves plead with the Lord for me, so that none of the things you have spoken may come upon me.”
Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I, then, take Christ’s members and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!
Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For He says, “The two will become one flesh.”
But the one who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with Him.
Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body.
Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? And you are not your own,
for you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.
Son, attend to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my words,
so that you may guard good understanding. I command you to heed the discernment of my lips.
Do not attend to a base woman, for honey drips from a prostitute’s lips; for a time she oils your throat.
Afterward, however, you will find it more bitter than gall and sharper than a two-edged blade.
For folly’s feet lead those who engage with her down with death into Hades; her tracks are not firmly set.
For she does not travel life’s ways; her tracks are slippery and not easy to recognize.
Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth.

Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
Do not be much involved with another woman, nor be held in the arms of one who is not your own.
For a man’s ways are before God’s eyes, and He watches all his tracks.
Lawless acts hunt a man, and each is bound tight by the cords of his own sins.
He dies among the undisciplined; from the abundance of his own life he was cast out and perished through folly.
I sought the Lord, and He heard me; from all my sojourns He rescued me.
Approach Him and be enlightened, and your faces will certainly not be put to shame.
This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him; from all his afflictions He saved him.
An angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear Him and will rescue them.
One who loves discipline loves discernment, but one who hates rebukes is foolish.
Better is the one who has found favor with the Lord, but a lawless man will be passed over in silence.
A person will not prosper through a lawless person, but the roots of the righteous will not be uprooted.
A courageous woman is a crown to her husband; but as a worm in wood, so a woman who does evil destroys a man.
Will not all these take up a parable against him and a riddle for his account? They will say, ‘Woe to the one multiplying for himself what is not his—how long?—and heavily weighting his collar!’
For suddenly those biting him will rise, and those plotting against you will awake; you will become their plunder.
Because you despoiled many nations, all the remaining peoples will despoil you, because of human bloodshed and impiety against land, city and all its inhabitants.
O you who acquire evil gain for your house, setting your nest on high to escape the hand of evils!
You planned shame for your house, brought many peoples to an end, and your soul sinned.
For a stone will cry from a wall, and a beetle from wood will utter these things.
For her captivity will be saved through judgment and through mercy.
The lawless and sinners will be shattered together, and those abandoning the Lord will be brought to an end.
For they will be ashamed of their idols, which they themselves wanted, and they were disgraced by their gardens, which they desired.
For they will be like a terebinth that has shed its leaves, like a garden that has no water.
Their strength will become a stalk of tow and their works sparks of fire. The lawless and sinners will be burned together, with no one to quench.”
Better is one who begins to help the heart than one who promises and leads it into hope; for a good desire is a tree of life.
One who despises a matter will be despised by it, but one who fears a command is sound.
Nothing good will belong to a deceitful son, but a wise household servant’s actions will prosper, and his way will be made straight.
The law of a wise person is a fountain of life, but the senseless will die by a trap.
Good understanding gives favor, and knowing the law belongs to a good mind, but the ways of the contemptuous are in destruction.
One who disciplines evil people will receive dishonor for himself, and one who reproves an impious person will bring blame on himself.
Do not reprove evil people, so that they may not hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
Give a wise person a starting point, and he will be wiser; inform a righteous person, and he will receive still more.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of holy ones is understanding.
For knowing the law belongs to a good mind.
For in this way you will live a long time, and years of your life will be added to you.
Son, if you become wise for yourself, you will also be wise for your neighbors; but if you turn out evil, you alone will bear evils.
when I went out early in the city, and my chair was set in the squares.
Young men saw me and hid, and all the elders stood.
Powerful men stopped speaking, placing a finger upon their mouths.
Those who heard called me blessed, and their tongues clung to their throats.
For an ear heard and called me blessed, and an eye that saw me turned aside.
For I rescued a poor person from a powerful man’s hand and helped an orphan who had no helper.
May the blessing of the perishing come upon me, and a widow’s mouth blessed me.
I had clothed myself with righteousness, and I wrapped myself in justice like a double cloak.
I was an eye for the blind and a foot for the lame.
I was a father to the powerless, and I traced out a case I did not know.
I crushed the molars of unjust people and tore the plunder from between their teeth.
